title: A constructive solution to the $n$-representability problem
authors: Nicholas C. Rubin, A. Eugene DePrince
abstract: We present a solution to the fermionic quantum marginal problem by constructing the complete family of two-body witnesses at each level of a weighted sum-of-squares hierarchy. Our construction combines positive-semidefinite Gram matrices with explicit linear nullspace constraints that exactly cancel all higher-body contributions, replacing the search for individual representability conditions with a systematic algebraic procedure. Beyond the completeness proof, we demonstrate the construction numerically by solving the associated semidefinite program and recovering the exact ground-state energy of a Richardson Hamiltonian in the three-fermion sector. We further prove that higher-degree particle-number multipliers are unnecessary when the full sum-of-squares generating algebra is used. These results establish a unified constructive framework for verifying the physicality of a candidate two-particle reduced density matrix through a complete characterization of all two-body witnesses.
summary: This paper provides a constructive, algebraic solution to the challenging $n$-representability problem in fermionic quantum systems. By systematically constructing a complete set of two-body witnesses using weighted sum-of-squares hierarchies, the authors offer a powerful tool to verify the physical validity of candidate reduced density matrices. This advances the theoretical understanding of many-body quantum simulations.
main_problem: The paper addresses the $n$-representability problem, which is determining the physical constraints on two-particle reduced density matrices (2-RDM) derived from an $n$-fermion state.
main_result: The authors establish a unified, constructive algebraic framework using weighted sum-of-squares (SOS) hierarchies to systematically verify the physicality of candidate 2-RDMs.
method: They construct a complete family of two-body witnesses by combining positive-semidefinite Gram matrices with explicit linear nullspace constraints derived from the canonical anticommutation relations.
model_or_system: The theory applies to fermionic quantum systems, relevant for quantum chemistry and condensed matter simulations, and is tested using the Richardson Hamiltonian in the three-fermion sector.
key_observables: Two-particle reduced density matrices (2-RDM), ground-state energy, and the set of two-body witnesses.
important_parameters: The degree of the SOS hierarchy ($d$), the number of fermions ($n$), and the specific Hamiltonian structure (e.g., Richardson).
main_assumptions: The initial SOS argument only required non-negativity on the fixed-$n$ subspace, and the constructed set $\Sigma_{d, \le 2}$ is noted to be incomplete for fixed-particle simulations.
figures_summary: TABLE I summarizes quadratic-generator Gram blocks resolved by changes in particle number and spin projection, detailing the structure of these blocks.
paper_structure: The paper develops from defining the $n$-representability problem, constructing the SOS hierarchy using Gram matrices and nullspace constraints, proving the equivalence between the SOS representation and the nullspace conditions, and finally applying this framework to derive energy bounds.
why_interesting: The rigorous algebraic framework for verifying physical constraints on reduced density matrices is fundamental to accurately simulating strongly correlated electron systems where approximations often fail.
